Title: Johor health exco warns of scam using his identity
Article:
JOHOR BARU: Johor Health and Environment Committee chairman Ling Tian Soon said that an irresponsible party had hacked his account on an app on his smartphone.
In a Facebook post, he said several acquaintances had contacted him after receiving a voice message this afternoon.
"Earlier, several of my friends received a voice message purportedly from me, saying there was an emergency matter.
"The individual also said he wanted to borrow money.
"When asked to make a phone call, the individual contacted my friend, but his voice sounded suspicious," he said.
He said the individual's accent sounded like that of someone from China.
"I want to stress that I have never asked anyone to lend me money.
"I urge all my friends and acquaintances to be more careful.
"Do not make any transactions or readily trust messages and calls using my identity.
"I hope everyone takes note and helps spread the word so that no one falls victim to this scam," he said.

Title: Ringgit ends higher against major currencies, easier vs greenback
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit ended higher against a basket of major currencies but slid against the US dollar on Thursday, as the greenback remained well supported despite waning expectations of an interest rate hike by the United States (US) Federal Reserve (Fed).
At 6pm, the ringgit fell to 4.0830/4.0875 against the US dollar from Wednesday's close of 4.0785/4.0820.
Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid noted that the ringgit traded in a narrow range of RM4.0820-RM4.0875 against the US dollar today.
"The odds of a US rate hike have gone down to below 50 per cent from more than 70 per cent previously, following the release of the latest personal consumption expenditures (PCE) inflation rate data, which was below market expectations.
"Despite that, the US dollar remains well supported with the US dollar Index rising by 0.30 per cent to 101.759 points," he told Bernama.
On that note, he said there appeared to be a possibility that the Fed might pause its rate hike in October, while markets continued to adjust to the latest PCE inflation rate.
Against major currencies, the ringgit rose against the euro to 4.6015/6066 from 4.6324/6363 at Wednesday's close, appreciated against the British pound to 5.3896/3955 from 5.4162/4209 yesterday, and firmed against the Japanese yen to 2.5781/5811 from 2.5969/5993 previously.
As for Asean currencies, the ringgit strengthened against the Singapore dollar to 3.1856/1894 from 3.1943/1973 at Wednesday's close, appreciated against the Thai baht to 12.1111/1294 from 12.1521/1666 yesterday, and inched up against the Philippine peso at 6.50/6.51 from 6.51/6.52 previously.
The ringgit was little changed against the Indonesian rupiah at 227.2/227.6 versus 227.9/228.2.

Title: Bidor shooting: Police take statements from nine witnesses
Article:
IPOH: Perak police have recorded statements from nine people, including the victim, in their investigation into the shooting of a businessman at a petrol station in Bidor Sentral last Tuesday.
Perak police chief Datuk Mohd Alwi Zainal Abidin said those whose statements were recorded included three family members who were in the victim's vehicle, two people in a vehicle near the scene and employees of the petrol station.
He said the victim is now in stable condition after receiving treatment and undergoing surgery at Seri Botani Hospital, while police are investigating from various angles, including identifying the motive, which has yet to be established.
"So far, police have not been able to determine the exact motive for the incident. Once we establish the motive based on the investigation, we will announce it," he told reporters at the Perak Police Senior Officers' Mess here today.
Mohd Alwi said police suspected that three individuals were involved in the incident, including a driver, while the registration number of the vehicle used by the suspects was believed to be fake.
He said police had also obtained closed-circuit television (CCTV) footage from the petrol station, which showed the victim being shot from two angles, from the front and the right side.
"We also reviewed CCTV footage at toll plazas and elsewhere, but what we found was that they did not exit the toll.
"However, we are still examining various angles to identify the suspects," he said.
Police are also investigating the possibility that the victim was being followed, based on the movement of the suspects' vehicle, which was driven at high speed before stopping in front of the victim's vehicle and opening fire.
According to Mohd Alwi, the victim is a businessman who owns a restaurant and runs several businesses around Bidor, Sungai Siput and Tapah.
In
the incident
, the victim, who sustained a single gunshot wound to the left shoulder, was sent to Tapah Hospital for initial treatment.

Title: Sarawak sees improved air quality as unhealthy readings fall
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Four areas recorded
unhealthy Air Pollutant Index
(API) readings as of 5.30pm today, down from 10 areas recorded earlier in the day.
Johan Setia in Selangor recorded the highest reading at 154, followed by Klang (139), Nilai in Negri Sembilan (130) and Putrajaya (122), according to the Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS).
Meanwhile, 57 areas nationwide recorded moderate readings.
Selangor's Shah Alam recorded 98, followed by Banting (97), Petaling Jaya (91) and Kuala Selangor (76), while in Negri Sembilan, Port Dickson recorded 95 and Seremban 93.
In Kuala Lumpur, Cheras recorded 96 and Batu Muda 89, while Melaka recorded readings of 90 in Bandaraya Melaka, 88 in Bukit Rambai and 81 in Alor Gajah.
Johor recorded moderate readings in Pasir Gudang (76), Segamat (72), Larkin (71), Kota Tinggi (69), Pengerang (66), Tangkak (66), Batu Pahat (65) and Kluang (57).
In Perak, Seri Manjung recorded 76, Tanjung Malim 66, Taiping 65, Pegoh Ipoh 63 and Tasek Ipoh 61.
In the east coast, Pahang's Balok Baru Kuantan recorded 82, Indera Mahkota Kuantan 71, Rompin 67, Temerloh 65 and Jerantut 56.
Terengganu recorded 78 in Kuala Terengganu, Kemaman (72), Paka (70) and Besut (66).
Kelantan recorded 73 in Kota Baru and 66 in Tanah Merah, while Penang's Seberang Perai recorded 63, Minden (61), Seberang Jaya (60) and Balik Pulau (54).
Up north, Kedah's Langkawi read 59, Sungai Petani (58), Alor Star (54) and Kulim Hi-Tech (51).
In Sarawak, Serian and Sri Aman recorded 65 and 63 respectively, followed by Samarahan (63), Samalaju (58), Kapit (56), Bintulu (55), Sarikei (52) and Kuching (52).
Sarawak has been affected by haze since early August, with smoke from peat fires in neighbouring Kalimantan contributing to the poor air quality.
Sabah recorded moderate readings in Tawau (78), Sandakan (70), Politeknik Kota Kinabalu (67), Keningau (54) and Kimanis (53), while Labuan recorded 53.
An API reading of 0 to 50 indicates good air quality, 51 to 100 moderate, 101 to 200 unhealthy, 201 to 300 very unhealthy, and 301 and above hazardous.

Title: 8 cops arrested in Taman Keramat ketum raid
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Eight cops and a man were arrested in a raid on suspected ketum activities in Taman Keramat here on Tuesday night.
A source said the arrests followed intelligence gathered by police, which led to an integrated operation.
"A team of policemen from the Bukit Aman Integrity and Standards Compliance Department's Intelligence and Operations Branch, assisted by the Ampang Jaya district police headquarters' Narcotics Criminal Investigation Division, raided a premises in Jalan AU 1, Taman Keramat, at 8.45pm.
"Eight lower-ranking police officers were arrested during the raid.
"Seven of them are attached to various units under the Sentul district police headquarters, while another is attached to the Brickfields district police headquarters. A civilian was also arrested at the scene," the source said.
The suspects are being held at the Hulu Kelang police station lock-up.
Investigation papers have been opened and police have applied for a remand order to facilitate further investigations under Section 30(3) of the Poisons Act 1952.
Bukit Aman's Integrity and Standards Compliance Department director, Datuk Aida Abdul Hamid confirmed the arrests.
She said the department was closely monitoring the case and that the investigation was being conducted transparently by the Ampang Jaya district police headquarters.

Title: KKB Engineering lands RM517mil Sarawak water job
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: KKB Engineering Bhd has bagged a RM517 million contract from the government through the Regional Corridor Development Authority (Recoda) for the Samalaju Phase 2 water supply infrastructure project in Sarawak.
In a bourse filing, the engineering company said it accepted the contract under the Sarawak Corridor of Renewable Energy with a completion period of 36 months.
KKB is also required to enter into a formal written agreement with the Malaysian government for the project.
The company expects the contract to contribute positively to its earnings and net assets, as well as those of the group, throughout the project's duration.

Title: Anwar joins pit lane walk ahead of Sepang F1 return
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today joined a pit lane walk at the Sepang International Circuit ahead of the  Formula 1 (F1) Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix, which returns to Malaysia this weekend.
Anwar was seen walking through the busy pit lane as teams made final preparations for the race, with mechanics, equipment and activity around the garages offering a close-up look at preparations ahead of the race weekend.
He was accompanied by Youth and Sports Minister Dr Mohammed Taufiq Johari and Chief Secretary to the Government Tan Sri Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar.
The pit lane walk gave guests an opportunity to get a closer look at the paddock and garage areas ahead of track action from Oct 2 to 4.
Yesterday, SIC chief executive officer Azhan Shafriman Hanif said the
circuit is fully prepared
ahead of the race, with nearly 100,000 tickets sold, setting a record for the highest ticket sales in the history of races held at the circuit.
Azhan said about 3,000 tickets still remained, comprising grandstand and hillstand seats, which could still be purchased online via bahraingp.com.

Title: IDEAS urges institutional reforms in 2027 Budget
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A public policy think tank has urged the government to make institutional reform a priority in 2027 Budget, including laws on political financing and election offences.
"Institutional reform cannot wait for another budget cycle. The government must prioritise enactment of institutional reforms," the Institute for Democracy and Economic Affairs (IDEAS) said in a statement.
IDEAS said relevant agencies, including the Legal Affairs Division of the Prime Minister's Department, Attorney-General's Chambers, Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission and Election Commission, should be adequately funded to advance institutional reforms.
On fiscal resilience, Ideas called for a broader and more sustainable revenue base, a transparent framework for Petronas dividends and higher productive development expenditure, particularly for energy transition and infrastructure.
"2027 Budget must respond to the immediate pressures of the Middle East energy shock while leaving Malaysia better prepared for the next crisis," it said.
IDEAS also urged a more predictable subsidy framework linked to global oil prices, alongside expanded targeted assistance such as Sumbangan Tunai Rahmah and Sumbangan Asas Rahmah.
On economic growth, Ideas said data-centre expansion should be tied to measurable economic benefits, including investment, employment, local procurement and stronger links with Malaysian companies.
On climate resilience, Ideas called for higher federal investment in climate mitigation and adaptation, proposing an increase from RM3.91 billion last year to at least RM5.50 billion.
The allocation would include funding for ecological fiscal transfers, local council drainage upgrades and district-level disaster preparedness.

Title: Sunway Healthcare confident after GIC exit
Article:
DAMANSARA: Sunway Healthcare Holdings Bhd is confident of continued investor support following the disposal of Singapore sovereign wealth fund GIC's remaining five per cent stake in the healthcare group.
Sunway Healthcare executive chairman Tan Sri Dr Jeffrey Cheah said the sale of about 575 million shares by GIC's investment vehicle, Greenwood Capital Pte Ltd, marked the final tranche of its holdings in the listed healthcare operator.
Cheah said a significant portion of the shares had been taken up by local institutions, including Permodalan Nasional Bhd and the Employees Provident Fund, reflecting continued institutional interest in Sunway Healthcare.
"They are a fund. Funds typically cannot hold (investments) for more than five years. When the time is up, they have to sell. That is their mandate.
"I think it is good that GIC does not have any more shares. I think it all goes well for stability in our share price," he said at the launch of Sunway Medical Centre Damansara here today.
Greenwood sold the shares at RM2.08 each, raising about RM1.2 billion, according to a Bloomberg report.
GIC's exit comes after it reduced its stake through Sunway Healthcare's initial public offering in March, which raised RM2.86 billion and was Malaysia's largest initial public offering (IPO) in almost a decade.
On Sunway Healthcare's expansion plan, Cheah said the company remained on track, including the development of three new hospitals by 2030.
The company's largest planned project is a hospital in Iskandar Puteri, Johor, with about 400 beds and an estimated capital expenditure of around RM800 million, he said.
"We also plan to develop hospitals in Seremban and Putrajaya, taking total planned capital expenditure for the three projects to about RM1.6 billion to RM1.7 billion," he said.
Meanwhile, as part of Sunway Healthcare's 2027 Budget wishlist, its president Datuk Lau Beng Long called on the government to ensure reasonable reimbursement rates for private hospitals under its ongoing healthcare reform initiatives.
Lau said private hospitals were particularly interested in ensuring that the eventual reimbursement levels under any reform were reasonable and reflected the cost of developing and operating private healthcare facilities.
"We hope that the programme will progress well because it's something that needs to be done.
"What the private hospitals will be interested in is the level of reimbursement that is finally agreed. It will be something that is reasonable, that will take into consideration the cost involved in developing private hospitals," he said.
Lau also called for greater government support for medical tourism, including assistance in developing healthcare manpower.
"Malaysia had an opportunity to attract more patients from countries such as Indonesia and Cambodia, where patients may seek treatment overseas.
"We hope more and more will choose Malaysia. And that's where the government can ensure that there's support for us," he added.

Title: Marine police arrest 2,707 in 7,627 maritime crime cases
Article:
PORT KLANG: Marine police have arrested 2,707 people in 7,627 criminal cases in the country's waters during the first nine months of this year.
Federal Internal Security and Public Order Department director Datuk Seri Mohd Yusri Hassan Basri said the arrests were the result of continuous enforcement efforts through various operations, including Op Taring Gelora, Op Taring Landai and inter- and intra-agency operations.
"From January to September, the team recorded seizures and fines worth RM525 million with the arrest of 2,707 people for various offences.
"The highest number of offences involved the Fisheries Act, with 3,214 cases, followed by offences under the Dangerous Drugs Act, Control of Supplies Act (295), Immigration Act and Anti-Trafficking in Persons and Anti-Smuggling of Migrants Act (213), as well as the Customs Act (189)," he said at a press conference after officiating the Marine Police 79th anniversary celebrations.
Yusri said the success was also attributed to effective bilateral cooperation and coordinated patrols with regional enforcement agencies from Thailand, Indonesia, Singapore and the Philippines.
On migrant smuggling, he said syndicates used various modus operandi to smuggle illegal immigrants into the country.
"They target international waters by transferring illegal immigrants to another boat before making a 'drop point' in Malaysia, with areas around Perak, Selangor, Johor and the northern part of the peninsula among their focus areas," he said.
Meanwhile, Yusri said the Marine Police had 22 projects under the Malaysia Plan, spanning the 11th to 13th Malaysia Plans, worth RM1.064 billion.
"For future strategic planning, it involves 19 proposed projects worth RM2.28 billion, including the construction of several operational bases for the team.
"The Marine Police will also receive two aircraft and five Fast Patrol Crafts, each worth RM100 million, to further strengthen the unit's capabilities in ensuring the safety of the country's waters," he said.
Earlier, Yusri presented the Marine Police 2026 Hero Award to former Sub-Inspector Jakarta Makling, 72, in recognition of his contributions and sacrifices during his service with the force.
Jakarta, when met, expressed his deep emotion over the award, which was introduced for the first time since he joined the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) on May 28, 1972.
"In June 1976, while serving as a patrol boat crew member, I was involved in a battle with a group of armed pirates in the waters of Lahad Datu, Sabah, and was shot in the left shoulder.

Title: Perkeso boosts benefits for more than 7mil contributors
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: More than seven million Social Security Organisation (Perkeso) contributors stand to benefit from enhanced Employment Insurance System (EIS) benefits that take effect today.
Perkeso said the improvements under amendments to the Employment Insurance System Act 2017 would provide an average benefit of about RM3,300 per person and help workers return to employment.
Among the changes is an increase in the Early Re-Employment Allowance to 50 per cent of the remaining Job Search Allowance, from 25 per cent previously, alongside higher training benefits and a new RM1,000 mobility allowance.
The maximum training fee has also been increased to RM7,000 from RM4,000, while the training allowance has been raised to RM30 a day, Perkeso said.
The amendments also introduce a new RM1,000 mobility assistance allowance, paid as a one-off benefit to contributors who lose their jobs, receive EIS benefits and secure new employment more than 100km from their homes.
Contributors who lose their jobs can submit applications online through the LINDUNG Kerjaya portal or at any Perkeso counter, it said in a statement.
Perkeso said the reforms were aimed at strengthening social protection amid changing labour market conditions and providing support for workers transitioning between jobs.
It said this would include job-matching services through the national employment portal MYFutureJobs, career counselling, reskilling and upskilling programmes, as well as mobility assistance.
"Perkeso will continue to strengthen MYFutureJobs by using labour market data and information to help contributors identify employment opportunities that match their skills, experience and industry needs.
"This approach is important to shorten the career transition period while ensuring workers' skills remain relevant to employers' needs and changes in the economic structure," it said.
The amendments to the Employment Insurance System Act 2017 received royal assent on Aug 30 and were gazetted on Sept 15.

Title: Johor to halt projects blamed for flash floods, mudflows
Article:
JOHOR BARU: Development projects in Johor found to have caused flash floods or mudflows in surrounding areas will be immediately shut down, said the state Housing and Local Government Committee.
Its chairman Datuk Mohd Jafni Md Shukor said action will be taken against developers and contractors who failed to comply with development approval conditions, particularly requirements for retention ponds and centralised drainage systems.
"Before any development begins, developers should build retention ponds and provide drainage systems according to the prescribed integrated guidelines.
"But the issue now is whether they build them or leave them until later.
"This often happens when developers appoint contractors focused on profit and rushing to complete projects, resulting in critical mandatory requirements being sidelined," told a press conference at Menara Majlis Bandaraya Johor Baru (MBJB) here.
Jafni said all housing and other development project developers in Johor Baru would be called for a briefing and stern reminder on flood mitigation requirements.
He said he had instructed the city council mayor to call all developers in the capital city to reinforce their responsibilities following the recent flooding.

Jafni said there would be no compromise with parties found violating regulations and causing hardship to residents.
He cited a recent case in Iskandar Puteri where a development project was ordered to stop work after a mudflow flooded a nearby housing area.
"The area had never flooded before. Suddenly, there was flooding and muddy water entered the nearby housing estate. When we investigated, it was confirmed that the development project was the source.
"Recently, we also stopped a project in Taman Lestari for 30 days to allow corrective works to be carried out.
"From now on, we will no longer just advise or negotiate. If we see earth-laden water flowing down and there is no other project in the area, we will take immediate action," he said.

Title: KKDW RM2.1 billion overspending issue resolved – Treasury deputy secretary-general
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: The issue concerning claims that the Rural and Regional Development Ministry (KKDW) had overspent RM2.1 billion against its allocations between 2023 and 2025 has been resolved, said Treasury deputy secretary-general (Policy) Datuk Zamzuri Abdul Aziz.
"It's already resolved," he told reporters after the launch of the Islamic Accounting Standards for Baitulmal, Zakat and Waqf (PPIBZW) programme.
He was responding to questions on the matter following a call by Umno Supreme Council member Datuk Razlan Rafii for Treasury Secretary-General Tan Sri Johan Mahmood Merican to explain the issue.
The issue arose following claims that KKDW spent RM1.8 billion in 2023 against an allocation of RM1.1 billion, RM2 billion in 2024 against RM1.3 billion and RM2.3 billion in 2025 against RM1.6 billion, resulting in a total deficit of RM2.1 billion.
On Sept 2, Johan explained that KKDW had made commitments and spent beyond its approved annual allocations for rural road projects.
He said the Finance Ministry (MoF) was working with KKDW to address the matter, including by restructuring the ministry's allocations based on priorities.
MoF also approved an additional RM300 million allocation for 2026 to help settle outstanding payments to contractors.

Title: Nepal move to verify status brings hope, relief to missing Malaysians' families
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Families of Malaysians still missing following last month's mudslide disaster in Nepal have welcomed the Nepali government's decision to expedite the process of verifying the victims' status.
Hani Othman, wife of Senior Fire Officer II Mohd Fakhrul Munir Mohd Isa, better known as Loe, said she was relieved by the decision after waiting for more than a month for certainty over her husband's fate.
She said she was still experiencing mixed emotions, holding on to hope that her husband would be found while recognising that the families also needed certainty over the status of those still missing.
"As a Muslim, I accept whatever Allah SWT has decreed and whatever the outcome may be. What matters is that we just want certainty about the status of those who remain unaccounted for.
"That way, we can make the necessary arrangements. I can settle whatever needs to be done on my husband's side and move forward with my life," she said when contacted today.
Hani also hoped the search and rescue (SAR) operation would continue as long as there remained a possibility of finding her husband and the other victims.
She said there had been no latest developments regarding the search, including the recovery of victims' belongings or the results of DNA tests.
Meanwhile, P.Sivan, 72, father of missing Rajita Sivan, said he appreciated the decision and hoped the next steps would proceed smoothly.
"This is a very sad tragedy. Unfortunately, the necessary certificates, including death certificates, have yet to be issued.
"Without these documents, we cannot process insurance claims or other compensation payments for the victims' families.
"I hope the Nepali government will give its full cooperation to the Malaysian government so that all matters can be resolved quickly, allowing the victims' families to receive the assistance and compensation they are entitled to without further delay," he said.
It was previously reported that the Nepal government had agreed to expedite the process of verifying the status of 55 Malaysians who remain unaccounted for following the disaster.
Government spokesman Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil had said that Nepal has agreed to help expedite the
process of confirming
the status of 55 Malaysians who remain untraced following the disaster in the country.
He said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim had spoken to his Nepali counterpart Balendra Shah, during which the latter agreed to the request.
The disaster in Nepal on Aug 26 claimed at least 1,453 lives, while 5,644 people were reported missing.
Of those still missing, 55 are Malaysians.

Title: Unemployed man jailed, fined RM3k for cheating e-hailing driver
Article:
JOHOR BARU: An unemployed man was jailed for five days and fined RM3,000 by the magistrate's court here for cheating an e-hailing driver with a fake payment receipt.
Magistrate A. Shaarmini imposed the sentence on B. Parameswara, 26, after he pleaded guilty to cheating Mohd Firdaus Md Naim by presenting the receipt.
The court ordered the jail term to run from the date of his arrest on Monday.
Parameswara was also ordered to serve an additional month in jail if he failed to pay the fine.
The accused had deceived Firdaus into believing that the receipt was genuine.
The offence was committed at a hotel in Jalan Bakawali 52, Taman Johor Jaya, here, on Sept 17.
Parameswara was charged under Section 417 of the Penal Code, which carries a maximum five-year jail term, a fine, or both upon conviction.
Deputy public prosecutor Anis Shafeeqah Mohd Sharifuddin prosecuted, while the accused was represented by lawyer P. Rajagunaseelan.

Title: Perodua Alza overturns after chain collision on Federal Highway
Article:
SHAH ALAM: Three vehicles were involved in a crash at Km14.1 of the Federal Highway heading from Klang towards Kuala Lumpur this morning.
The accident, which occurred around 7.20am, involved a Perodua Myvi, a Perodua Alza and an Isuzu D-Max.
The Myvi was travelling in the right lane and had slowed down due to traffic congestion ahead before it was hit from behind by the Alza.
The collision caused the Myvi to hit the D-Max in front, while the Alza skidded and overturned onto its left side.
No injuries were reported among the drivers of the three vehicles.
It is learned that the case is being investigated under Rule 10 of the Road Traffic Rules 1959, which carries a maximum fine of RM300.
Traffic flow returned to normal around 8am after the vehicles were removed from the scene.

Article:

Title: UK PM Burnham sows seeds of "Breturn" that could excite markets
Article:
NEVER mind Britain's stretched budget numbers. The real surprise this week was new Prime Minister Andy Burnham's push to re-engage with the European Union — including the possibility of rejoining.
It may matter far more for markets. Even a whiff of "Breturn" could move sterling assets.
Better EU relations have been in the policy mix since the Labour Party returned to power in 2024, but sweeping geopolitical events over the past 18 months, combined with a change of prime minister determined to pursue his core beliefs about how the country should be repaired, are now supercharging the idea.
If even Canada is now eyeing "associate" EU membership in a bid to rally the "Middle Powers", the risk that Britain could be adrift as rivalry between the world's economic and military superpowers intensifies is very real.
At his Labour Party's annual conference on Tuesday, Burnham, who campaigned to stay in the EU in a 2016 Brexit referendum, argued the nation should again consider options for "Britain's long-term relationship with our European partners."
He said all options from closer relations to rejoining the EU single market to re-applying for membership would be on the table for his party and the wider public to consider.
But instead of setting it aside on a long to-do list, Burnham doubled down on the idea in interviews right through Wednesday — re-emphasising that full reversal of Brexit was one of the options.
Britain can't decide this on its own, of course. EU governments have shown little appetite for reopening accession talks, domestic opposition remains vocal, and any transition would carry its own costs.
Moreover, any process could take many years. But the direction of travel could well excite investment and markets long before the destination.
At the core of Burnham's message was the most basic observation: "Brexit has done more harm than good."
More than a decade after the narrow referendum to leave the EU, that view has substantial support among the public and many economists.
With the referendum's anniversary marked in June, reams of analysis on the economic impact poured out.
While formal Brexit didn't happen until the height of the 2020 pandemic, making cause and effect hard to disentangle, the only real debate among economists now is how much the decision hit trade and gross domestic product (GDP) — not whether.
The Office for Budget Responsibility estimates range from a cumulative 4-percentage-point hit to UK productivity to a long-term lowering of 15 percentage points of imports and exports.
The total effect on British GDP is estimated at anywhere up to 6-8 percentage points.
[[nid:1545538]]
Even more benign scenarios — such as Deutsche Bank's "doppelganger" approach, which looks at how Britain might have performed if it hadn't left — see the cumulative GDP hit at as much as 4 percentage points.
That's before you get to the business and financial complications related to renewed barriers, red tape and movement restrictions between Britain and its biggest trading partner.
Even the loudest rallying cry of Brexit — to reduce immigration — didn't reduce overall numbers to any significant degree; it only shifted their origin.
Opinion polls show significant regret — underlining why Burnham may feel confident in broaching the issue politically.
A YouGov poll published early in September showed 55 per cent of respondents felt Brexit marked a "wrong turn" — compared with just 21 per cent who thought the opposite and 11 per cent who were equivocal.
A separate poll found some 55 per cent in favour of rejoining. And an Ipsos poll earlier in the year showed 52 per cent favoured re-applying for EU membership compared with 33 per cent who wanted to stay out.
It's true that Burnham's speech initially produced no financial-market fireworks. Bond markets were more focused on pension and social care reforms and other domestic initiatives, broadly applauded by commentators.
Helped by an upgrade to second-quarter GDP estimates, sterling was more buoyant on Tuesday against both the dollar and euro — and gilts may have surfed some of the Burnham momentum too.
After all, the pound was the biggest casualty of the 2016 referendum, with its effective exchange rate index plunging 14 per cent in just three months after the vote.
After a slow rebuild, it's taken a decade to get back close to where it was before the shock — even though it remains down about 10 per cent against the euro and dollar and still has a considerable gap to close.
A harder job will be to repair the widely worrying underperformance of UK equities over the past decade and what many still see as a gaping "Brexit discount" between UK stock valuations and those of euro zone counterparts — never mind Wall Street.
For some, Brexit, or its reversal, now seems as central to Britain's most pressing issues as welfare reform and defence. Burnham's intervention suggested a willingness to confront the really big questions rather than dancing around them.
Economist Anatole Kaletsky at GaveKal Research reckoned Burnham's speech may be seen as a pivotal moment for the UK economy and "a bullish inflection point for sterling assets."
"These are the great issues that will determine whether Britain prospers or stumbles in the decades ahead," he added.
A decade of confusion and loss of direction in Britain might be coming to a close — just as the rest of the world becomes harder to navigate.
* The writer is from Reuters

Title: Thunderstorm, heavy rain warning issued for KL, 10 states until 7pm
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a warning for thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds affecting Kuala Lumpur, Putrajaya, Labuan and 10 states until 7pm today.
In a statement, MetMalaysia said the adverse weather was expected to affect Kedah, Perak and Kelantan.
In Kedah, the affected areas are Kuala Muda, Sik and Baling, while in Perak, they are Hulu Perak, Selama, Kerian, Larut Matang, Kuala Kangsar, Hilir Perak and Bagan Datuk.
In Kelantan, the warning covers Kuala Krai and Jeli.
Similar warnings were issued for Terengganu, covering Kemaman, Dungun and Hulu Terengganu; Pahang, covering Rompin, Maran, Temerloh and Bera; and Selangor, covering Hulu Langat, Hulu Selangor, Kuala Selangor, Klang, Gombak, Petaling, Sepang and Kuala Langat.
In Negri Sembilan, the areas expected to be affected are Seremban and Port Dickson.
In Johor, the warning covers Segamat, Tangkak, Muar, Kluang, Batu Pahat, Johor Baru, Kulai and Pontian.
In Sarawak, the affected areas are Mukah (Matu, Dalat, Mukah and Daro), Sibu (Selangau and Sibu), Kapit (Kapit, Bukit Mabong and Song), Bintulu, Miri (Subis), Limbang, Sri Aman (Sri Aman, Pantu and Lingga), Samarahan, Betong, Serian and Kuching (Kuching).

Title: Afghan tourist's cause of death in Pulau Tioman pending lab analysis
Article:
ROMPIN: The cause of death of an Afghan tourist who fell unconscious while diving off Pulau Tioman yesterday remains undetermined pending laboratory analysis of post-mortem findings.
Rompin police chief Superintendent Sharif Shai Sharif Mondoi said the post-mortem, which began at Tengku Ampuan Afzan Hospital in Kuantan around 10am today, had yet to determine the cause of death.
"The medical team requires further laboratory assessments following several findings from the post-mortem examination.
"It could be related to drowning, but they need to rule out all other possibilities first before concluding that the victim drowned," he said in a statement.
In the 11.30am incident near Kampung Salang yesterday, Mohammed Seyar Musazay, 55, a civil engineer from California, was diving with his 24-year-old daughter when he appeared to be
struggling in the water.
Seconds later, the diving instructor noticed that his breathing regulator had fallen out of his mouth and that he was unconscious before rushing him to a clinic on the island, where he was pronounced dead.

Title: 'Loud thud': Sperm whale sinks yacht in South Pacific
Article:
WELLINGTON: A sperm whale cracked the hull of a yacht sailing in the remote South Pacific, forcing four sailors into a day-and-night fight for survival on the high seas.
Crew members on the 16-metre Tai Tam told AFP on Thursday of their weekend encounter with a pod of sperm whales 250 nautical miles north of tiny Norfolk Island.
"There was sort of a loud thud. The whole boat was pushed sideways," said Australian Jemma Cooper, who was thrown from the steering wheel by the force of the blow.
Not knowing at first what had happened, she noticed a brown discolouration in the water and a sperm whale.
"We looked out to our port side, and there were six to eight, a pod, of whales there. So then it became clear that that's what it was," she told AFP.
Her husband Jeremy Cooper said he was sleeping below deck when the impact woke him.
"It was pretty immediately evident it was very serious," he said.
"All the steering gear was smashed on the starboard side, and there was a significant amount of water coming in," Jeremy told AFP.
At 1 pm New Zealand time Saturday (2400 GMT Friday) – about 30 minutes after the whale collision – they activated an emergency beacon.
"We declared a full mayday," said New Zealand crew member Terry Hetherington, adding they spent the next few hours bailing out as much water as they could.
The Royal Zealand Air Force flew a P-8A Poseidon patrol plane to the area to establish radio communications and coordinate the rescue.
French crew member Martin Jaffre, a joiner, said the whale collision left several gashes in the hull and cracked the fibre glass structure, as well as breaking the steering.
"We could no longer steer the boat, and a boat with no steering quickly becomes a problem," he told AFP.
Jaffre battled to slow the incoming water with anything to hand, including expansion foam, and swam below the boat to inspect the hull, his crew mates said.
The sailors tried to stay aboard as long as possible, struggling to stop the engine getting clogged and bailing by hand.
Late at night, they abandoned the boat and transferred to a life raft in calm seas and under a full moon.
In the early hours of Sunday morning, they cut the tether to the yacht, fearing it might drag them down. Soon after, it slipped beneath the waves.
A 143-metre container ship, the MV Sofrana Surville, rescued the sailors at 6 am Sunday (1700 GMT Saturday), the New Zealand military said – about 18 hours after their encounter with the sperm whale.
Even the rescue was scary as the giant ship approached their tiny life raft, recalled Jeremy Cooper.
But within half an hour they had scaled a ladder to join their rescuers, have a cup of coffee and chat with the captain, he said, ruing the end of their Pacific holiday voyage.
"It was wonderful, wonderful, and just a terrible, terrible ending – but luckily no loss of life."

Title: Johor allocates RM30mil to tackle flash floods in city
Article:
JOHOR BARU: The Johor government will allocate an additional RM30 million to implement four immediate measures, covering short- and medium-term solutions, to address flash floods in the city.
State Housing and Local Government Committee chairman Datuk Mohd Jafni Md Shukor said the decision was reached at a special committee meeting following yesterday's unusual flash floods in several parts of the city.
He said rainfall recorded yesterday was exceptionally high, at two to three times the normal rate, reaching 60mm to more than 100mm in certain areas compared with the normal rate of 10mm an hour.
"Weather conditions are now difficult to predict. Although the Johor Baru City Council (MBJB) spent more than RM100 million over the past four years and has allocated another RM48 million for next year to upgrade pumps and embankments, the sheer volume of water makes it difficult for it to flow into the Straits of Johor.
"Therefore, we have identified four key areas that need to be implemented immediately to address the issue," he said at a press conference at Menara MBJB here today.
He was commenting on yesterday's flash floods that affected several areas, including Kampung Mohd Amin, Kampung Pasir and Jalan Ayer Molek.
Mohd Jafni said the four key measures included appointing specialists by MBJB to conduct a detailed study of the drainage system in the city, in line with a comprehensive district-level study by the Drainage and Irrigation Department (DID).
"We will also build an underground retention pond through an On-Site Detention (OSD) system at Jalan Sungai Chat.
"This involves excavating and constructing an underground concrete tank to hold water, while the space above can be used as a playground or car park, as has been implemented at Kota Iskandar.
"We will also increase the capacity of new water pumps discharging into the Straits of Johor in preparation for and to address unusually high rainfall over the next five years, as well as relocate mobile pumps to high-risk locations such as Kampung Pasir.
"In addition, we will upgrade and widen monsoon drains, including widening crossing culverts at critical locations with the construction of two 1.2-metre-diameter drains by the Public Works Department (PWD)," he said.
Mohd Jafni said several immediate measures would also begin tomorrow.
These include deepening the Kampung Mohd Amin retention pond by 0.9 metres and lowering existing water levels at retention ponds such as Taman Merdeka and Sungai Chat using scheduled pumping before heavy rain.
"This is aimed at providing greater flexible retention capacity to accommodate excess rainwater," he said.
At the same time, Mohd Jafni said integrated coordination meetings would be held weekly involving MBJB, DID, PWD and the Land and District Office to continuously monitor the progress of the flood mitigation projects.
Yesterday, media reported that several areas around Johor Baru were hit by flash floods following more than an hour of heavy rain in the afternoon.
Affected areas included Jalan Kolam Ayer, Taman Kolam Air; the Skudai Highway towards the city centre and Jalan Semangka, Kampung Seri Jaya.
Videos of several passenger buses being inundated by floodwaters along Jalan Yahya Awal here also went viral on social media.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Anwar thanks outgoing Chinese ambassador for strengthening bilateral ties
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim thanked the outgoing Chinese Ambassador to Malaysia, Ouyang Yujing, for his contributions towards strengthening ties between Malaysia and China.
Ouyang, the 16th Chinese ambassador to Malaysia, paid a farewell visit to Anwar today following the end of his tenure in Malaysia last September.
In a Facebook post, Anwar said Ouyang had demonstrated commitment and contributed towards strengthening cooperation between the two countries in various fields, including the economy, technology, education and culture.
"Malaysia and China have built a strong bond in various fields, including economy, technology, education, and culture," he said.
Anwar said strategic cooperation involving the East Coast Rail Link (ECRL), 5G technology, artificial intelligence (AI), ports and the rare earth industry had also opened new avenues for mutual benefit.
"Malaysia and China have built a strong bond in various fields, including economy, technology, education, and culture, and strategic cooperation such as ECRL, 5G technology, artificial intelligence, ports, and rare earth industries have also opened new avenues for mutual benefit," he said.
During the visit, Anwar was also gifted with a book about Hangzhou, the hometown of Chinese Premier Li Qiang, which Anwar visited last September.
"I also received a special gift from Premier Li Qiang in the form of a book about Hangzhou, which I recently visited and is his hometown.
"I greatly appreciate the memory and attention," he said.
Anwar said both countries would continue to strengthen their long-standing friendship and cooperation while exploring new areas for the benefit of the people, regional security and prosperity.
Earlier this week, Ouyang said
Malaysia-China relations
had undergone three major strides over the past five years, progressing from a Comprehensive Strategic Partnership to a China-Malaysia community with a shared future before reaching their current status.
He said the developments had opened broader prospects for cooperation, while President Xi Jinping's visit to Malaysia in April marked another milestone that ushered in a new "Golden 50 Years" for bilateral relations.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Iran Guards hail US withdrawal from Iraq as 'historic victory'
Article:
TEHERAN: Iran's Revolutionary Guards on Thursday welcomed the withdrawal of US forces from Iraq as a "historic victory" and called for American troops to leave the Middle East.
The Revolutionary Guards "congratulate the proud nation of Iraq, the united front of the Islamic Resistance, and the revolutionary fighters of the Islamic world on this historic victory," the guards said in a statement carried by their official media.
On Wednesday the US-led coalition that deployed to Iraq and Syria in 2014 to fight the Islamic State (IS) group formally concluded its mission and withdrew.
IS, which seized large swathes of both countries and committed massacres and atrocities, was defeated in Iraq in 2017 and in Syria in 2019, but coalition forces stayed on to battle the group's remnants.
"The US must leave the region and entrust the management of security to the nations themselves," said the statement by the Revolutionary Guards, the ideological arm of Iran's military.
"Two decades of occupation demonstrated that the US presence brought no security; rather, it was the very source of insecurity, terrorism, and instability in West Asia," it added.
Baghdad and Washington agreed in 2024 to wind down the coalition's mission, and its troops withdrew gradually from bases across the country, restricting their presence to the autonomous northern Kurdistan region.
The Iraqi government says the coalition's withdrawal removes the excuse powerful Iran-backed militant factions have used to retain their weapons.
On Thursday, Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi announced June 30 as a new deadline for armed factions to turn over their weapons to the state.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Gravedigger jailed a month for stealing RM16 from surau donation box
Article:
JOHOR BARU: A gravedigger was jailed a month by the magistrate's court here today for stealing RM16 from a surau donation box at a shopping mall.
Magistrate A. Shaarmini ordered Nazarudin Mahmud, 45, to serve the sentence from the date of his arrest.
Nazarudin stole the cash from the surau donation box at Angsana Johor Baru Mall at 4.20pm on Monday.
He was charged under Section 380 of the Penal Code for theft, which carries a maximum 10-year jail term and a fine upon conviction.
The court heard that Nazarudin was arrested after his actions were captured by the surau's closed-circuit television cameras.
He had used a metal ruler to pry open the donation box, and the stolen cash found in his possession when he was arrested.
Earlier, National Legal Aid Foundation lawyer Noor Asyikin Shafiqah Atham Malik appealed for a lighter sentence, saying it was Nazarudin's first offence and his guilty plea had saved the court's time and costs.
She also told the court that Nazarudin, who suffers from epilepsy, earned about RM1,500 a month and supported his 75-year-old mother.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Saravanan questions MACC over son's presence at headquarters
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Former Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri M. Saravanan has criticised the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission's (MACC) explanation for his 12-year-old son's presence at its headquarters on Monday, describing it as "entirely illogical".
Saravanan said there was no reason to involve a minor, adding that it was regrettable for an agency with significant investigative powers to fail to exercise basic discretion and common sense when dealing with a 12-year-old child.
MACC chief commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman said today that the commission did not serve an asset declaration notice on Saravanan's 12-year-old son.
He said the boy's presence at the MACC headquarters was as a companion to his parents and not to receive an asset declaration notice.
"The chief commissioner's claim that the children 'had no one left at home' and therefore 'came along as usual' is both irrelevant and dismissive.
"It deflects from the administrative oversight of requiring a minor to set foot at an anti-corruption headquarters for official investigative procedures," he said.
Saravanan and his family members went to the MACC
headquarters
in Putrajaya on Monday to receive the asset declaration notices.
The notices were issued as part of MACC's ongoing investigation into Saravanan over alleged corruption linked to the approval of foreign worker quotas.
Earlier, Halim said the
agency
had exercised its discretion and "considered what was reasonable" in deciding not to serve an asset declaration notice on Saravanan's son.
He said the 12-year-old's presence at the MACC headquarters did not mean he was there to receive a notice in connection with the investigation.
Saravanan, however, questioned why such discretion had not been exercised earlier.
He said requiring a child to be served a legal notice in person crossed the line of reasonable enforcement and reflected an excess of statutory power.
He had raised concerns before going to the MACC headquarters with his family on Monday.
He said the asset declaration notice purportedly meant for his son could instead have been served through him as the boy's parent.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 35 years, 12 strokes for man who robbed, raped and murdered woman
Article:
TAWAU: A man who pleaded guilty to murdering a roti canai maker was sentenced to 35 years in prison and 12 strokes of the cane by the High Court here today.
Judicial Commissioner Steve Ritikos imposed the sentence on Md Ridzuan Abd Ahmad Zaini Logan, 37, after considering submissions by the prosecution and defence on the appropriate sentence.
Deputy public prosecutor Nur Nisla Abd Latif had sought the death penalty or, alternatively, the maximum 40-year prison sentence.
In her submission on aggravating factors, she said that although the Abolition of Mandatory Death Penalty Act 2023 had come into force, the death penalty could still be imposed in certain cases, citing several court decisions in which the death penalty had been imposed after the Act came into force.
She said the circumstances surrounding the victim's death were particularly cruel and horrific, based on evidence and photographs from the scene.
She also highlighted the suffering the victim was alleged to have endured, noting that she had only returned to work about six months after giving birth to help supplement her family's income before her death.
The prosecution also submitted that there were no factors such as mental incapacity or grave and sudden provocation that could be considered mitigating circumstances in the case.
However, lawyer Kamarudin Mohmad Chinki, representing Md Ridzuan, sought a 30-year prison sentence and 12 strokes of the cane, taking into account his client's guilty plea, remorse, background and family responsibilities.
The defence submitted that the death penalty did not necessarily have to be imposed in every murder conviction and that the court should assess the circumstances of each case and the offender's background individually.
After considering submissions from both sides, the court sentenced Md Ridzuan to 35 years in prison and 12 strokes of the cane, with the sentence backdated to his date of arrest on Nov 17, 2024.
According to the charge, Md Ridzuan murdered Sirlin Salleh, 36, in a bushy area in Kampung Pisang, Lahad Datu, between 6am and 8am on Nov 14, 2023.
He was charged under Section 302 of the Penal Code.
Meanwhile, as Md Ridzuan was being led out of the courtroom after the decision was delivered, Kamarudin offered words of encouragement to his client, urging him to repent and perform more religious acts while serving his sentence.
Media reports previously said the woman, who worked as a roti canai maker, was not only robbed and raped but also murdered before her body was found in a bush.
The 36-year-old woman was found partially clothed by family members at about 8.15am after her employer noticed that she had not turned up for work.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Pupil who suffered broken leg after being slammed by ustaz wins appeal, awarded RM47,000
Article:
KUALA TERENGGANU: A pupil who suffered a broken right leg after being slammed by an ustaz during a Kafa class has won his appeal at the High Court, more than four years after the incident.
The Kuala Terengganu High Court ordered the ustaz and Yayasan Islam Terengganu (YIT) to pay Muhammad Izz Anaqi Mohd Izwan, now 13, RM30,000 in general damages, RM17,000 in costs and five per cent annual interest from the date the suit was filed until full settlement.
Lawyer Mohd Hazwan Hamidun said the High Court allowed his client's appeal against the Kuala Terengganu Sessions Court's decision to dismiss the claim.
"The case was initially filed at the Sessions Court, but the court dismissed the plaintiff's claim. Today, the High Court allowed the appeal and awarded RM30,000 in damages together with RM17,000 in costs.
"The total is almost RM47,000, excluding interest from the date the suit was filed until full settlement," he said after the proceedings.
According to Hazwan's law firm, Rafaei & Co, the incident occurred around 3.30pm on July 6, 2022, when Izz Anaqi was 9, and attending a Kafa class at SK Tasek, Marang.
In a statement, the firm said Ustaz Ahmad Mursyidin Abdullah held and lifted the pupil before slamming him onto a wooden chair, causing injuries to his right leg.
The pupil suffered fractures to the tibia and fibula in his right leg, as well as other fractures, leaving him unable to walk and requiring a cast. He was also unable to attend school for almost three months.
The suit was filed at the Kuala Terengganu Sessions Court on Jan 9, 2023, through his mother, Nor Azlina Mohamad Yasin, as guardian ad litem, against Mursyidin and YIT.
Sessions Court judge Wan Aklima Wan Salleh dismissed the claim on Feb 16 this year, prompting the family to appeal to the High Court.
Hazwan said the High Court found that the Sessions Court judge had erred in assessing the evidence of two eyewitnesses who were in the same class and witnessed the incident.
"The court also took into account a medical report by specialists at Hospital Sultanah Nurzahirah, which confirmed that the pupil's leg injuries were caused by a strong impact.
"YIT, as the ustaz's employer, was also vicariously liable for the injuries suffered by our client," he said.
The pupil is now in Form One at a boarding school.
His father, Mohd Izwan Ahmad Saidi, 40, said the family had endured emotional distress for more than four years before the court decision.
"After almost four years, justice has finally been served for my son.
"I am grateful to the team of lawyers who worked to ensure justice was achieved for my son," he said.
He said the ruling also answered the accusations and insults directed at his son and family throughout the period.
"With justice having been achieved, all the accusations and insults hurled at our family have finally been answered through the justice secured by the lawyers," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Afghanistan says deadly Pakistani strikes hit Helmand
Article:
KABUL: The Pakistani military launched rare deadly strikes on Afghanistan's Helmand province on Thursday, the Taliban government and residents told AFP.
Afghanistan and Pakistan went to war earlier this year and, with no permanent resolution to security issues reached, there have been sporadic attacks since a March truce.
The latest strikes hit Helmand as well as Kunar, which borders Pakistan, killing 10 civilians, according to the Taliban government's deputy spokesman Hamdullah Fitrat.
Islamabad confirmed "planned and calibrated" strikes in Afghanistan, without detailing locations, which it said targeted militants.
Two Helmand residents told AFP that three airstrikes hit their village.
Pakistan's information ministry said two locations in Afghanistan were hit "based on credible intelligence, selective targeting of terrorist camps and hideouts."
Alongside neighbouring Kandahar province, which was hit by an airstrike last week, Helmand in southern Afghanistan holds great importance for the Taliban movement.
Speaking by phone from Helmand's Safar village, 50-year-old resident Abdul Wahid said the strikes killed four people and wounded seven.
Another villager, Qudrat Ullah, said he was home when his neighbours' house was hit.
"The whole area is destroyed," the 32-year-old said, adding that residents were being kept away from the strike sites.
"There were civilians, children, women; they have killed them. There is no military or anything else," he told AFP by phone.
Pakistan's information ministry reported an initial toll of 22 militants killed, and weapons and ammunition destroyed.
Islamabad accuses Afghanistan of harbouring militants behind frequent bomb and gun attacks in Pakistan, which have killed both civilians and security personnel.
The Taliban government denies this and criticises Pakistan for violating Afghanistan's sovereignty and killing civilians.
In mountainous Kunar province, an AFP journalist saw the remains of stone houses in the remote Chugam Valley.
Mohammad Hashim, a farmer, said he rushed to rescue residents after the pre-dawn attack.
"There was a woman, she was screaming for help to get her out of the rubble. She was having trouble breathing and told us that there are more people over there," the 30-year-old told AFP.
"We went there to dig, and there was a man with four children who were killed," he added.
The latest strikes follow bombardment last week on multiple Afghan provinces, which the Taliban government said killed civilians. Pakistan said it targeted militants.
More than 500 civilians have been killed in violence between the two countries since October, according to figures from the United Nations mission in Afghanistan.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Don't abuse your power, deputy IGP tells police
Article:
KUCHING, Oct 1 — Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) leaders have been reminded not to abuse their positions and instead carry out their responsibilities with integrity, accountability and fairness.
Deputy Inspector-General of Police Datuk Seri Abdul Aziz Abdul Majid said leadership was not a privilege to be used for personal gain but a major trust that must be discharged responsibly.
“Therefore, I urge that every decision made must be based on integrity, accountability and a sense of fairness,” he said at the handover ceremony for the Sarawak acting police commissioner and acting chairman of the Sarawak Contingent Persatuan Keluarga Polis (Perkep) at the Sarawak Police Contingent Headquarters here today.
Earlier, he witnessed the handover of duties from PDRM Management Department director Datuk Mohamad Zainal Abdullah, who was also the Sarawak police commissioner, to his deputy DCP Saifullizan Ishak before Mohamad Zainal begins his duties at Bukit Aman.
Abdul Aziz also reminded leaders not to oppress or mistreat their subordinate officers and personnel, but to guide, listen to and protect those under their charge.
He said leadership based on such values was important in creating a fair, harmonious and respectful working environment. — Bernama

Title: Malaysia’s marine police nab 2,707, record 7,627 cases in national waters this year
Article:
PORT KLANG, Oct 1 — The Marine Police Force (PPM) arrested 2,707 individuals in 7,627 criminal cases in the country’s waters during the first nine months of this year.
Bukit Aman Internal Security and Public Order Department (JKDNKA) director Datuk Seri Mohd Yusri Hassan Basri said that the success was the result of continuous enforcement through various operations such as Op Taring Gelora, Op Taring Landai, and inter or intra-agency operations.
“From January to September, the team recorded seizures and fines worth RM525 million with the arrest of 2,707 people for various offences.
“The highest offences among them involve the Fisheries Act 1985 with 3,214 cases, the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952 (428), the Control of Supplies Control Act 1961 (295), the Immigration Act 1959/63 and the ATIPSOM Act 2007 (213), as well as the Customs Act 1967 (189 cases),” he said at a press conference after officiating the 79th Anniversary celebration of the PPM at the Region One PPM Operations headquarters, Pulau Indah here today.
Mohd Yusri said that the success was also the result of effective bilateral cooperation and patrol coordination with regional enforcement agencies such as Thailand, Indonesia, Singapore and the Philippines.
Commenting on the issue of illegal immigrant smuggling, he said that irresponsible parties use various modus operandi to infiltrate the country.
“They are targeting international waters by transferring illegal immigrants to another boat before making a ‘drop point’ to Malaysia, with the focus areas including waters around Perak, Selangor Johor, and the northern part of the Peninsula,” he said.
Meanwhile, Mohd Yusri said that PPM as a whole now has 22 projects under the Malaysia Plan (11MP to 13MP) worth RM1.064 billion.
“For future strategic planning, it involves the application of 19 proposed projects worth RM2.28 billion, including the construction of several operational bases for the team.
“PPM will also receive two aircraft carriers and five Fast Patrol Crafts, each worth RM100 million, to further strengthen the unit’s capability in ensuring the safety of the country’s waters,” he said.
Earlier at the event, Mohd Yusri presented the PPM 2026 Hero Award to Sub Inspector (B) Jakarta Makling, 72, in recognition of his contributions and sacrifices throughout his service in the force.
Jakarta, when met, expressed deep emotion over the award that was introduced for the first time since he joined the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) on May 28, 1972.
“In June 1976, while serving as a patrol boat crew member, I was involved in a battle with a group of armed pirates in the waters of Lahad Datu, Sabah, and was shot in the left shoulder.
“The bullet still remains in my shoulder to this day and serves as a testament to my sacrifice in carrying out my duty to protect the safety of the nation’s waters,” said the grandfather of 13 from Semporna, Sabah. — Bernama

Title: Malaysia plans A-to-D food grades to nudge manufacturers — and consumers — towards healthier choices
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 1 — Malaysia could introduce a new food labelling system giving packaged food and drinks nutrition grades from A to D by the end of this year, Health Ministry official Dr Yap Wei Aun has said.
Dr Yap, chief executive officer of the Health Ministry’s Health Transformation Office, said prevention was a fundamental aspect of public health and cited the proposed labelling system as an example of the government’s preventive health initiatives.
He said the labels could help nudge Malaysians towards healthier food choices without relying on individual willpower alone, while also encouraging the food and beverage industry to reformulate products to make them healthier.
“At the population level, I’m a little bit less convinced that we can depend on willpower and education to really drive lifestyle change,” he said yesterday during the “Innovating for Retirement Wellbeing” panel session at the Employees Provident Fund’s (EPF) International Social Wellbeing Conference (ISWC) 2026.
Dr Yap said the Health Ministry had been working with partners, including the food industry, to introduce the “front-of-pack labelling” system, under which bottles of drinks or packaged food would carry an A, B, C or D grade.
An A grade would represent the healthiest option, while D would indicate the least healthy.
“So now does it depend on the person per se? Actually, the main effect of this is behaviour change happening at the industry level, in terms of reformulating these foods so that they meet the A and B criteria, rather than the C and D criteria.
“And then when these foods go out, you don’t even depend on consumer choice, prices, availability. The whole health environment has changed,” he said, adding that the approach would reduce reliance on public education alone.
“So, we were collaborating, there’s a terms of reference and a committee jointly with Singapore, because we realised that we share the same food environment. And hopefully this will be rolled out,” he said.
“So we are aiming for gazettement probably end of the year,” he added.
Dr Yap said the measure was among initiatives being developed to address major health risks including physical inactivity and mental health, as well as dietary risks in Malaysia involving “too much salt, too much sugar, and too much calories overall”.
Although the new labelling system may appear to be primarily a “consumer choice” initiative, he said it could work alongside other public health policies to encourage healthier lifestyles by changing the wider food environment.
“Imagine if you are a school — you can just decide we will only serve A and B in the school compound. If you are doing government procurement, if you are an employer, you are only going to make A and B available,” he said.
He said other measures could include restricting advertising for less healthy products and changing how food is presented in retail spaces.
File photo of Health Minister Datuk Seri Dzulkefly Ahmad, whose ministry is developing a mandatory Nutri-Grade system to classify food and drinks according to their nutritional content. — Picture by Choo Choy May
Nutri-Grade in Malaysia and Singapore
While Dr Yap did not use the term “Nutri-Grade” to describe the front-of-pack labelling system, Singapore currently uses the term, which has also previously been cited by Health Minister Datuk Seri Dzulkefly Ahmad in relation to Malaysia’s plans.
In a written parliamentary reply on October 27, 2025, Dzulkefly said Malaysia already had a voluntary front-of-pack food labelling system known as the Healthier Choice Logo (HCL), which assesses nutritional components including fat, salt and sugar content.
At the time, 1,002 food and beverage products had received HCL recognition.
In the same reply, Dzulkefly said Malaysia was developing a mandatory Nutri-Grade system based on sugar levels in drinks, which would be introduced in stages, beginning with ready-to-drink products before being extended to freshly prepared beverages.
Under the proposed system, Dzulkefly said advertising would be completely banned for drinks given a D grade — those containing more than 10g of sugar per 100ml — on any platform.
He said the measure was intended to encourage manufacturers to reformulate their products and reduce sugar levels.
Dzulkefly said Malaysia’s Nutri-Grade system was initially focusing on the sugar content of drinks because the National Health and Morbidity Survey (NHMS) 2024 showed an increase in sugar intake among Malaysians, with more than half of free-sugar intake coming from beverages.
According to the World Health Organisation, free sugars include those added to food and drinks by manufacturers, cooks or consumers, as well as sugars naturally present in honey, syrups, fruit juices and fruit juice concentrates.
In Singapore, the
Nutri-Grade system
assigns drinks grades from A to D based on their sugar and saturated fat content.
Nutri-Grade labels are mandatory for drinks graded C and D, while advertising for products given a D grade is prohibited.
